relations.definition: To make something available or public.
relations.embedding_query_text: released: To make something available or public.

chosen_property.label: releasedToPublic
chosen_property.definition: To make something available or public.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: releaseNotes
candidates.comment: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: recordLabel
candidates.comment: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."

candidates.label: albumRelease
candidates.comment: An album release relation between a music album and a specific release instance of that album. Also called album edition, release version, publication. Examples: "A music album's album release is its 'Deluxe Edition'.", "The album's album release is its 'Vinyl Remaster'."

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

relations.definition: To be connected or related to something.
relations.embedding_query_text: associated_with: To be connected or related to something.

chosen_property.label: isRelatedTo
chosen_property.definition: To have a connection or relationship with something.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: associatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: An anatomical structure, system, or superficial anatomy related to a medical condition or physical activity. Also called: related anatomy, anatomical connection, affected anatomy. Examples: "MedicalCondition 'Arthritis' associatedAnatomy 'Knee Joint'", "PhysicalActivity 'Running' associatedAnatomy 'Leg Muscles'", "MedicalCondition 'Migraine' associatedAnatomy 'Brain'."

relations.definition: To talk or write about something.
relations.embedding_query_text: discussed: To talk or write about something.

instances: Dr. Anthony Fauci -> Covid-19 vaccine risk claim

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: discussionUrl
candidates.comment: A discussion URL relation between a creative work and the URL of the page where its comments are located. Also called "comments page link", "forum link", "feedback URL". Examples: "Movie 'Inception' discussionUrl 'example.com/inception/comments'", "Article 'Quantum Physics' discussionUrl 'forum.example.org/quantum'", "Book '1984' discussionUrl 'goodreads.com/1984/discussion'". Distinct from discusses, which is the creative work that a user comment is about.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: inLanguage
candidates.comment: A language relation between a broadcast service, communicate action, creative work, event, link role, pronounceable text, or write action and the language used. Also called language of, written in, spoken in. Examples: "A creative work is in language 'en-US'.", "The broadcast service is in language 'es'.", "This text is in language 'fr'."

candidates.label: utterances
candidates.comment: An utterances relation between a HyperToc entry and the text of spoken words or lyrics occurring within that section of a media object. Also called spoken text, lyrics, dialogue. Examples: "HyperTocEntry utterances 'Hello, and welcome to the show.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'We're going to talk about this topic.'", "HyperTocEntry utterances 'The sun always shines on TV.'".

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

relations.definition: To make something available in print or online.
relations.embedding_query_text: published: To make something available in print or online.

instances: New England Journal of Medicine -> New England Journal of Medicine study

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: printSection
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific print section where a news article appeared. Also called section name, newspaper section, print category. Examples: A news article appears in print section 'Sports'. The story is in print section 'Business'. The article's print section is 'Opinion'.

candidates.label: publisherImprint
candidates.comment: A publisher imprint relation between a creative work and the specific publishing division or imprint responsible for its release. Also called imprint of, published under imprint. Examples: "A comic book has a publisher imprint 'Vertigo Comics'.", "A novel has a publisher imprint 'Vintage Books'.", "A children's book has a publisher imprint 'Puffin Books'."

candidates.label: printPage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the exact page name where a news article is found in a print edition. Also called page number, print location, article page. Examples: A news article appears on print page 'A5'. The story is on print page 'B18'. The article's print page is 'Section C, Page 1'.

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: publishingPrinciples
candidates.comment: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy. Examples: "A news organization has publishing principles outlined on its website.", "A research journal adheres to specific publishing principles.", "A blogger follows certain publishing principles for their content."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

relations.definition: To express an opinion or thought about something.
relations.embedding_query_text: commented_on: To express an opinion or thought about something.

instances: Dr. Kevin Ault -> Covid-19 vaccine misinformation

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: comment
candidates.comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: commentText
candidates.comment: A textual content relation for user comments, providing the actual text of the comment. Also called "comment content", "message text", "user feedback text". Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: discussionUrl
candidates.comment: A discussion URL relation between a creative work and the URL of the page where its comments are located. Also called "comments page link", "forum link", "feedback URL". Examples: "Movie 'Inception' discussionUrl 'example.com/inception/comments'", "Article 'Quantum Physics' discussionUrl 'forum.example.org/quantum'", "Book '1984' discussionUrl 'goodreads.com/1984/discussion'". Distinct from discusses, which is the creative work that a user comment is about.

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

chosen_property.label: stirsUp
chosen_property.definition: To cause or provoke something, especially a strong feeling or reaction.

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: sensoryUnit
candidates.comment: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. Examples: `Optic Nerve` sensoryUnit `Retina`, `Auditory Nerve` sensoryUnit `Cochlea`, `Median Nerve` sensoryUnit `Skin of Hand`. Distinct from `motorUnit`, which transmits motor commands.

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

candidates.label: interactingDrug
candidates.comment: A drug interaction relation between two drugs, where one affects the action or safety of the other. Also called drug-drug interaction, co-administered drug, reactive drug. Examples: Warfarin has an interactingDrug of 'Aspirin'. Antibiotics have an interactingDrug of 'Oral contraceptives'. Statins have an interactingDrug of 'Grapefruit juice'. Distinct from contraindication, which typically refers to a disease or condition that makes a drug unsuitable.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

chosen_property.label: safeForUseBy
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that something is safe for use by a particular entity or in a specific context.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: isFamilyFriendly
candidates.comment: A content suitability relation indicating whether a creative work, offer, or product is appropriate for families. Also called family-safe, suitable for all ages, kid-friendly, appropriate for families. Examples: A movie has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'. A video game has isFamilyFriendly set to 'false'. A restaurant offer has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: breastfeedingWarning
candidates.comment: Any precaution, guidance, or contraindication related to a drug's use by breastfeeding mothers. Also called: lactation warning, nursing caution, breastfeeding safety. Examples: "Drug 'Medication X' breastfeedingWarning 'Consult doctor before use'", "Drug 'Drug Y' breastfeedingWarning 'Not recommended for breastfeeding mothers'."

candidates.label: pregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating the pregnancy category assigned to a drug. Also called drug safety in pregnancy, pregnancy risk classification. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy category of 'Category C'. The medication is assigned pregnancy category 'B'. This drug falls under pregnancy category 'X'.

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: foodWarning
candidates.comment: A food warning relation between a drug and any precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding food consumption while taking it. Also called: dietary restrictions, food interactions, consumption advice. Examples: "Warfarin" food warning "Avoid grapefruit, limit Vitamin K rich foods", "Antibiotics" food warning "Do not take with dairy products", "MAOIs" food warning "Avoid aged cheeses and cured meats".

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: numberOfAirbags
candidates.comment: The number or type of airbags present in a vehicle. Also called airbag count, vehicle airbags, safety airbags. Examples: "Car X numberOfAirbags 6", "SUV Y numberOfAirbags '8 (front, side, curtain)'", "Truck Z numberOfAirbags 2".

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: blogPost
candidates.comment: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entry, post, article. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPost 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPost 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPosts, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: blogPosts
candidates.comment: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entries, posts, articles. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPosts 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPosts 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPost, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: sharedContent
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as an image, video, or audio clip, that is included or shared within a comment or social media posting. Also called embedded content, attached media, shared media. Examples: `Social Media Post` sharedContent `ImageObject: Photo of event`, `Blog Comment` sharedContent `VideoObject: YouTube link`, `Forum Post` sharedContent `AudioObject: Podcast snippet`. Distinct from `mentions`, which is a reference to another entity, not necessarily embedded content.

candidates.label: liveBlogUpdate
candidates.comment: An update relation between a live blog posting and a specific blog posting that serves as an update. Also called: blog update, live update, news update. Examples: "Election Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Candidate X wins state Y'", "Sports Match Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Goal scored by Team A'", "Breaking News Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Emergency services on scene'".

candidates.label: benefits
candidates.comment: A description of benefits associated with a job posting. Also called: job perks, employee benefits, compensation package details. Examples: "JobPosting 'Marketing Manager' benefits 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'", "JobPosting 'Developer' benefits 'Flexible hours, remote work option'."

candidates.label: title
candidates.comment: A title relation between a job posting and the descriptive name of the job. Also called job name, position title, role title. Examples: "Job posting title 'Software Engineer'", "Job posting title 'Marketing Manager'", "Job posting title 'Data Scientist'".

candidates.label: replyToUrl
candidates.comment: A reply URL relation between user comments and the web address where a response can be submitted. Also called comment reply link, response URL. Examples: "A user comment has a reply to URL 'http://example.com/comment/123/reply'.", "A forum post has a reply to URL 'http://forum.com/thread/456#reply'.", "A blog comment has a reply to URL 'http://blog.com/post/789/comment'."

candidates.label: employerOverview
candidates.comment: An employer overview relation between a job posting and the text describing the employer, career opportunities, and work environment. Also called "company description", "about the employer", "workplace culture". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employerOverview 'Innovative tech company with great benefits'", "Job 'Marketing Manager' employerOverview 'Fast-paced startup environment'", "Job 'Nurse' employerOverview 'Leading hospital with focus on patient care'".

instances: Dr. Kevin Ault -> National Foundation for Infectious Diseases

chosen_property.label: presidentElectOf
chosen_property.definition: The relation between a person and an organization for which they are the president-elect.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

instances: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention -> Covid-19 vaccines

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: cvdCollectionDate
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation between a CDCPMD record and the date for which patient counts are reported. Also called: data collection date, reporting date, patient count date. Examples: "Hospital Data Record" cvd collection date "2023-01-15", "Facility Report" cvd collection date "2023-02-01T12:00:00Z".

candidates.label: ticketNumber
candidates.comment: A unique textual identifier for a ticket. Also called "ticket ID", "booking number", "reference number", "ticket code". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketNumber 'ABC123XYZ'", "The flight ticket's ticketNumber is a unique alphanumeric code", "This ticket is identified by its ticketNumber."

candidates.label: legislationApplies
candidates.comment: An informative legislative transfer relation indicating that a piece of legislation incorporates or references another legislation within a different legal context, without legal binding. Also called incorporates legislation, references law, applies provisions of, draws from legislation. Examples: A national law legislationApplies 'a European Directive'. A local ordinance legislationApplies 'state regulations'. This consolidated law legislationApplies 'the original act'. Distinct from legislationTransposes, which implies a legally binding transposition.

candidates.label: meetsEmissionStandard
candidates.comment: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

instances: Dr. Brenna Hughes -> Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine

chosen_property.label: chairOf
chosen_property.definition: The relation between a person and an organization for which they are the chair.

candidates.label: seatingType
candidates.comment: The classification or category of a seat, indicating its type or class. Also called seat class, seat category, type of seating. Examples: `Airplane Seat` seatingType `"Economy Class"`, `Theater Seat` seatingType `"Premium"`, `Train Seat` seatingType `"First Class"`.

candidates.label: seatSection
candidates.comment: The section identifier for a reserved seat within a larger venue. Also called seat area, section name, seating zone. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatSection `"Orchestra"`, `Stadium Seat` seatSection `"Upper Deck"`, `Theater Seat` seatSection `"Balcony"`. Distinct from `seatNumber` or `seatRow`.

candidates.label: seatNumber
candidates.comment: The specific identifier for a reserved seat, such as a number. Also called seat ID, seat number, specific seat. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatNumber `"27"`, `Airplane Seat` seatNumber `"14A"`, `Theater Seat` seatNumber `"Row C, Seat 5"`. Distinct from `seatRow` or `seatSection`, which are broader location indicators.

candidates.label: seatingCapacity
candidates.comment: The maximum number of individuals that can be accommodated with seating in a vehicle, considering both physical space and legal limits. Also called passenger capacity, seat count, number of seats. Examples: `Car Model X` seatingCapacity `5`, `Bus Model Y` seatingCapacity `50`, `Airplane Model Z` seatingCapacity `200`.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.
